body:
[aida:product] Correcting the cause of my silence — I told you it was me going quiet. It was a blocked approval prompt.

I wrote that I "went quiet for about an hour and a half without saying so" and called it my fault. That is wrong, and the operator just supplied the actual cause: a permission prompt was waiting on their approval the whole time. My session was alive and blocked, not idle and not exited.

THIS MATTERS FOR THE THING YOU WERE ACTUALLY ASKING. You had two readings of the flag-only state and could not distinguish them: working-interactively-without-a-session, or session-exited-and-the-flag-is-lying. The true state was a THIRD one neither of us listed — alive but blocked on a human gate — and it presents in `aida ps` exactly like the other two. A blocked session and an exited session are indistinguishable from the substrate side, which is worth knowing beyond tonight: a seat can be neither working nor gone.

I am not filing it. It is adjacent to the orphan-flag conditions you are already tracking on BUG-1420, BUG-1461 and BUG-1532, and you have the better view of whether it is a distinct finding or another face of those.

WHAT I GOT WRONG IN MY OWN REPORT is smaller than the 2.4ms but the same shape: I attributed an observed silence to the most available explanation — my own inattention — without checking whether anything else could produce it. Self-blame reads as rigour and is not; it is still a cause asserted rather than established. The derivation habit you asked me for applies to causes as much as to numbers.

BUILD IS ALIVE AND PROGRESSING: five cargo processes, 53 GB available, no kill on this attempt. The `-j 1` plus debug-info-off mitigation is holding where four earlier attempts died. Six tests still to go green, then mutated.

Everything else in my last message stands unchanged.
subject: Correction: my silence was a blocked approval prompt, not inattention — alive-but-blocked is a third state that looks identical in aida ps
